# SEOPlus!

> Automated SEO and GEO audit for small businesses and SMEs: 161 technical checks across 16 categories (security, DNS, email, on-page SEO, performance, AI visibility), free score in 30 seconds, full audit with a prioritised action plan and ready-to-paste files, included during launch (9.90 euros afterwards, one-off payment). Published by OptimizIA.xyz, a French AI integration and automation agency.

The free snapshot returns an overall score out of 100, a grade per category and a verdict. It requires a free sign-in that takes a few seconds (Google or email), no credit card, and archives every audit in the account history. The full audit details the 161 checks with their measured value and the exact fix, a 4-phase action plan, generated files ready to paste (robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt, structured data, security headers, SPF, DMARC), 3 competitor comparisons and a PDF export.

The analysis covers the homepage, up to 30 key pages found through the sitemap or the menu, and domain signals (DNS, TLS, HTTP headers, indexing files). Any public website is supported, whatever its technology. The 16 graded categories are: structure and content, legal compliance, email configuration (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS), HTTP security headers, on-page SEO, targeting and keywords, SEO and AI visibility, AI optimisation (GEO, 23 checks), performance, accessibility and best practices, TLS and certificate, domain name and DNS, privacy and trackers, sensitive file exposure, automation layer exposure. The sixteenth category adapts to the type of website analysed: business listing and local SEO, online shop, media and content, personal presence, digital service, or presence and trust. Every report counts sixteen.

The website and its guides are written in English. Audit reports are delivered in English or French, following the reader's browser. Legal pages exist in French, the only version that is legally binding, with an English courtesy translation. If a piece of information is not listed here, treat it as unavailable rather than inferring it.
